section_summary: This section contains U.S. State Department, military, and SCAP correspondence and intelligence reports from April 1947 through December 1949 regarding Japanese base metals, mining resources, and metallurgical policy. Major subjects include bauxite exploitation in the Pacific Mandated Islands, reparations and alumina processing proposals involving Reynolds Metals and Permanente Corporation, and pricing agreements for antimony and ferroalloy exports. The documents also address control and intelligence inquiries concerning strategic and radioactive materials, including impounded uranium oxide, beryllium stocks sought by the Atomic Energy Commission, domestic titanium ore and refining capacity, and iron ore purchases from Hainan.

subfiles.about: Inquires whether the UN Security Council trusteeship decision permits formulating policy on bauxite mining in the Japanese Mandated Islands.
subfiles.from: G. R. Parker, Chief, Pacific Ocean Division, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.summary: Parker asks whether the Security Council trusteeship decision will clarify policy on bauxite mining in the Japanese Mandated Islands.
subfiles.title: Letter from G. R. Parker to Edwin M. Martin Regarding Bauxite Mining in the Japanese Mandated Islands
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: States that commitments regarding private trade and bauxite exploitation in the Mandated Islands remain premature pending congressional action.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Martin advises that commercial bauxite exploitation in the Mandated Islands is premature pending congressional approval and establishment of island government.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to G. R. Parker Regarding Bauxite Mining in the Mandated Islands
subfiles.to: G. R. Parker, Chief, Pacific Ocean Division, U.S. Commercial Company

subfiles.about: Requests transmission of agreed Japanese antimony pricing formulas to British representatives in Tokyo to conclude a pending export transaction.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Whitman requests that agreed antimony pricing formulas be forwarded to British representatives in Tokyo to finalize a 484.95-ton antimony shipment.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Mr. Willson Regarding Japanese Antimony Pricing
subfiles.to: Mr. Willson, Raw Materials Section, British Embassy, Washington

subfiles.about: Inquires about the future status of Japan's aluminum industry prior to visiting Aluminium Limited in Canada.
subfiles.from: Dr. Hans Tiedemann
subfiles.summary: Tiedemann asks for information on the future status of Japan's aluminum industry before meeting with Aluminium Limited in Canada.
subfiles.title: Letter from Hans Tiedemann to Hugh Borton Regarding Future Status of the Japanese Aluminum Industry
subfiles.to: Dr. Hugh Borton, Chief, North-East Asian Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: Outlines the Far Eastern Commission's May 13, 1946 policy decision on interim reparations removals in Japan's light metals industry.
subfiles.from: Hugh Borton, Chief, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Borton details Far Eastern Commission policy declaring primary aluminum and magnesium capacity available for reparations, while retaining 15,000 tons fabrication capacity.
subfiles.title: Letter from Hugh Borton to Hans Tiedemann Regarding Far Eastern Commission Light Metals Reparations Policy
subfiles.to: Hans Tiedemann

subfiles.about: Reiterates Far Eastern Commission interim reparations policy concerning Japanese light metals and aluminum fabricating capacity.
subfiles.from: Hugh Borton, Chief, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Borton retransmits the Far Eastern Commission interim reparations policy decision regarding light metals removals and Japanese aluminum capacity retention.
subfiles.title: Letter from Hugh Borton to Hans Tiedemann Regarding Far Eastern Commission Aluminum Policy
subfiles.to: Hans Tiedemann

subfiles.about: Expresses State Department reservations concerning proposals to process imported alumina and bauxite in Japanese aluminum plants.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Saltzman advises against premature rehabilitation of Japanese aluminum plants for processing American or Dutch East Indies raw materials, urging that any arrangements protect reparations allocations and FEC policy.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles E. Saltzman to William H. Draper, Jr., Regarding Aluminum Processing in Japan
subfiles.to: William H. Draper, Jr., Under Secretary of the Army

subfiles.about: Transmits Under Secretary of the Army Draper's letter concerning alumina shipments to Japan for review and reply.
subfiles.from: C. W. Lewis, Office of Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Routing memorandum transmitting Under Secretary Draper's March 5 letter on alumina processing in Japan for a reply if necessary.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from C. W. Lewis to Roswell H. Whitman Regarding Processing of Alumina in Japan
subfiles.to: Roswell H. Whitman, Office of Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Discusses inquiries by Reynolds Metals Company and Permanente Corporation to reduce alumina in Japan, awaiting reports from SCAP.
subfiles.from: William H. Draper, Jr., Under Secretary of the Army
subfiles.summary: Draper reports on discussions with Reynolds Metals and Permanente Corporation regarding alumina processing and exports from Japan, noting no official proposals have been received from SCAP.
subfiles.title: Letter from William H. Draper, Jr., to Charles E. Saltzman Regarding Aluminum and Alumina Proposals for Japan
subfiles.to: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Records interagency agreement that SCAP should continue central impoundment of uranium oxide in Japan rather than release it to industry.
subfiles.from: C. A. Wendel, Office of the Under Secretary, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Conferees agreed that uranium oxide impounded by SCAP should not be released to Japanese industry to protect security operations.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Impounded Uranium Oxide in Japan
subfiles.to: Department of State

subfiles.about: Receipt confirming delivery of top secret memorandum of conversation regarding uranium oxide in Japan.
subfiles.from: R. Gordon Arneson, Office of the Under Secretary, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Receipt of classified material signed by C. W. Lewis for the top secret uranium oxide memorandum of conversation.
subfiles.title: Receipt of Classified Material for Memorandum of Conversation on Uranium Oxide
subfiles.to: C. W. Lewis, Office of Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Inquires on behalf of the Atomic Energy Commission whether SCAP holds stocks of beryl ore, beryllium compounds, or beryllium metal in Japan.
subfiles.from: Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army (CSCAD)
subfiles.summary: Army cable relaying Atomic Energy Commission request for information on any post-occupation beryl ore or beryllium stocks held by SCAP.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Classified Message WAR 81765 to SCAP Regarding Beryllium Stocks in Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo (SCAP)

subfiles.about: Transmits a proposed draft cable to SCAP requesting information on stocks of beryllium in Japan on behalf of the Atomic Energy Commission.
subfiles.from: Alexander L. Keyes, Office of Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Keyes transmits a draft cable requesting that SCAP report to the Atomic Energy Commission on stocks of beryl ore and beryllium metal in Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Alexander L. Keyes to Civil Affairs Division Transmitting Draft Cable to SCAP on Beryllium Stocks
subfiles.to: Executive Officer, Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army

subfiles.about: Requests that the Department of the Army cable SCAP to determine whether stocks of beryl ore or beryllium are held in Japan.
subfiles.from: C. A. Wendel, Office of the Under Secretary, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Wendel requests Keyes to arrange an Army cable asking SCAP whether post-occupation beryl ore or beryllium stocks exist in Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from C. A. Wendel to Alexander L. Keyes Regarding Beryllium Inquiry
subfiles.to: Alexander L. Keyes, Office of Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Receipt confirming delivery of secret memorandum from Wendel to Keyes concerning beryllium in Japan.
subfiles.from: C. A. Wendel, Office of the Under Secretary, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Form receipt acknowledging delivery of secret memorandum from Wendel to Keyes regarding the Atomic Energy Commission beryllium inquiry.
subfiles.title: Receipt of Classified Material for Memorandum on Beryllium
subfiles.to: Alexander L. Keyes, Office of Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Transmits data furnished to the Norwegian Diplomatic Mission regarding Japanese ferroalloy productive capacity, historical production figures, and export prices.
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (Cloyce H. Boehringer)
subfiles.summary: Despatch reporting information provided by SCAP to the Norwegian Diplomatic Mission on Japanese ferroalloy capacities, export price quotations, and annual production statistics for 1935 through 1948.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 370: Information on Production of Ferroalloys in Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Central file sheet recording receipt of an August 8, 1949 letter from Far East Air Forces regarding the availability of titanium in Japan.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Document file note recording an August 8, 1949 letter from Far East Air Forces concerning titanium availability in Japan.
subfiles.title: Document File Note Regarding Availability of Titanium in Japan
subfiles.to: Department of State

subfiles.about: Transmits Fifth Air Force indorsement and intelligence report detailing Japanese titanium sand ore deposits, refining plants, and production methods.
subfiles.from: Major B. J. McKinnis, Acting Chief, AIR Section, Headquarters, Far East Air Forces
subfiles.summary: McKinnis forwards intelligence including a Fifth Air Force indorsement and technical report on Japanese titanium sand zones, oxide extraction plants, and refining companies.
subfiles.title: Letter from Far East Air Forces Transmitting Intelligence Reports on Titanium in Japan
subfiles.to: Headquarters, United States Air Force, Attention: Director of Intelligence

subfiles.about: Central files record form designating a replacement copy of Telegram C 54034 from Tokyo for official filing.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Form designating a replacement copy of incoming Telegram C 54034 from Tokyo for permanent central records filing.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Form for Telegram C 54034 from Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of State Central Files

subfiles.about: Reports that the contract between E. Ott Company and MITI for Hainan iron ore will not be renewed due to unsettled conditions in China.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo (SCAP)
subfiles.summary: SCAP reports that MITI will not renew its Hainan iron ore contract with E. Ott Company, shifting to ship-by-ship purchases.
subfiles.title: Telegram C 54034 from SCAP Tokyo Regarding Hainan Iron Ore Contract
subfiles.to: Secretary of State and Chief of Staff, United States Army
